[[Category:Measure theory| 2]]
A '''measure space''' is a [[measurable space]] $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$ equipped with a '''measure''' $\mu$. 

== Definition ==

=== Measure ===

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(X)$ be a [[measurable space]], then [[function]]

$$
\mu:\mathcal F\to[0,\infty]
$$

satisfying:

* '''Null empty set''': $\mu(\varnothing)=0$;
* '''Countable additivity''': $\mu\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}A_i\right)=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\mu(A_i)$ for [[pairwise disjoint sets]] $A_1,A_2,\dots\in\mathcal F$,

is a '''measure''' of $(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(X))$.

=== Measure space ===

The triple

$$
(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)
$$

is then a '''measure space'''.
